# Barrel generation

Read when a package's generated `src/index.ts` barrel, its `exportsGeneration` option, or the ctix invocation behind them is in question. This page holds the whole rule; `SKILL.md` keeps only the index line.

## Barrels are generated by the build, not in front of it

`getTsdownConfiguration` runs ctix from a `build:prepare` hook, so no manifest repeats the command. What a package generates is the `exportsGeneration` option — `"typescript"` by default, `"vue"` for the package that ships components, `"none"` for one that names its own entrypoints and would otherwise get a barrel nothing is an entry for. `export:gen` regenerates a barrel without a build, and runs that same hook's function through the `generate-exports` bin `@esposter/configuration` declares: a manifest names the bin and passes the answer (`generate-exports vue` in the package that ships components), never a ctix config path. `ctix` is a devDependency of `@esposter/configuration` alone, resolved from there rather than found on `PATH`.

Two things make it work, and both look redundant until they are gone:

- **`entry` is stated even though it is tsdown's own default.** Left unset, tsdown treats the default as a glob and resolves it _while resolving the config_, before any hook runs — so a package whose barrel is not on disk dies with `No input files`, which is every fresh clone. A literal entry reaches rolldown, which reads it after `build:prepare`.
- **The option is a union of literals, never an enum.** `packages/configuration` reaches its own source through `#src/*`, and tsdown loads a config with Node's strip-only type stripping: an enum fails outright with `TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode`. A type erases to nothing.
- **The bin reaches that source through `#src/*` too, never the built `dist`.** `export:gen` exists to regenerate a barrel without a build behind it, so a bin importing `dist` needs the build it was meant to skip: a fresh clone has no `dist` until something builds it, and the barrel that build wants is the one the bin was asked for. A subpath import resolves against the manifest that declares it, so the same specifier works from whichever package invoked the bin.

Generation is **unguarded** — ctix runs on every build. A barrel of `export * from` names no symbol, so it reads as a function of the source file list and nothing else, which is what makes a hash-and-skip guard look obvious. It is not one, and the reason is worth knowing on its own: ctix resolves two files exporting the same identifier by **dropping both from the barrel**, printing a `detect same name of export statement` warning and exiting 0 — a case-conflicting filename is its only non-zero exit. So a rename that creates a collision changes what ctix writes while moving no path and adding no file, which a key over the file list cannot see. It is also the one way a package loses a public export with every check green: `publint`, `attw`, `deps.onlyImport` and typecheck all pass, because none of them knows what the barrel _should_ have held, and the warning scrolls past inside a whole-workspace build. What prevents that is the naming convention rather than a check — one export per file, named after the file (`file-organization`, `naming`) — and don't add a guard over the barrel to catch it either, because asserting over generated output fails on a fresh clone instead of on the regression (`testing`). What makes the absent skip cost nothing is the `package-builds` cache, which restores `dist` and the barrels together on an exact content hash; a build that misses it is regenerating every package regardless.

**Watch generates a barrel once, at start.** tsdown calls `build:prepare` inside its single build pass and only then hands the graph to rolldown's watcher, so no rebuild under `watch:packages` runs ctix again — and the restart it does have is keyed on the entry glob changing, which a literal `entry` can never trigger. An edit to an existing file therefore flows through; a **new** file's export does not, and a sibling resolving the `source` arm reads a barrel that never learned about it. `pnpm export:gen` in that package rewrites the barrel, which is itself a graph file and so triggers the rebuild that picks it up — restarting the watch is the other answer.
